title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-07-21
content:
Applied ML weekly research notes — 2026-07-21
Owner: Aisha Kapoor (eng-applied-ml)
Collaborators: Liam Chen, Rafael Gomez, Marta Novak
Status: in_review

Summary
- This week focused on two parallel threads: finalizing an int8/4-bit quantization profile for the 7B instruction-tuned model (rt-7b-instr) and running a lightweight eval pass to catch regressions before onboarding the new model bundle to hosted API.
- We have a working quantization pipeline that preserves instruction-following quality within 2–3% relative drop (measured on our instruction-eval suite) while reducing GPU memory by ~55% and improving steady-state throughput by ~1.8x.
- Remaining risks: occasional prompt-dependent decoding artifacts at 4-bit extreme quantization; need larger eval sweep and a focused adversarial prompt set.

Goals for next week
- Complete extended eval sweep across instruction-eval, MMLU subset, and factuality checks (deadline: 2026-07-28).
- Harden fallback policy in the router for quantized variant (implement latency-based routing + model-similarity check) — owner: Liam (due 2026-07-30).
- Run on-device (Dedicated) smoke tests with the quantized bundle on T4 and A10 pools — owner: Rafael (due 2026-07-27).

Quantization workstream (Aisha + Rafael)
- Experiments run: FP16 baseline vs int8 (symmetric/asymmetric) vs 4-bit GPTQ-like path.
- Tools: internal quantization toolkit (qtool v0.9), calibration on 2k instruction prompts, per-channel weight quantization for attention layers.
- Results (summary):
  * FP16 baseline: peak GPU memory 14.2GB, throughput (tokens/s) 420 at batch=8
  * int8 (symmetric): peak memory 7.1GB, throughput 760 tokens/s, instruction-eval delta -1.6%
  * 4-bit (gptq hybrid): peak memory 6.0GB, throughput 830 tokens/s, instruction-eval delta -3.1% with spikes on long-context factual prompts
- Notes: Int8 is the current sweet spot for production; 4-bit gives additional density but introduces rare decoding issues (likely quantization noise amplifying during softmax). Rafael to open a spike PR to log-layerwise activations for failing prompts (github PR linked above).
- Action items:
  * Add adversarial prompt set (50 prompts) that triggers decoding artifacts to nightly evals (owner: Aisha, 2026-07-24).
  * Add per-layer clipping and bias-fine-tune step (lightweight 500-iters) for worst-offender layers to mitigate 4-bit failures (owner: Rafael, 2026-07-29).

Evals & CI (Liam + Marta)
- Evals run were automated via eval-harness v0.9.7 with new evaluator scripts for instruction-following (IF-score), factuality (F1 on fact-check dataset), and hallucination classifier AUC.
- Key results:
  * IF-score (higher is better): FP16=0.78, int8=0.765, 4bit=0.755
  * Factuality F1: FP16=0.72, int8=0.71, 4bit=0.68
  * Decoding hallucination AUC: FP16=0.91, int8=0.90, 4bit=0.86
- Regression detection: two failing tickets added to JIRA-APPL-212 (one for a reproducible hallucination case, one for a prompt-specific repetition loop).
- CI integration: new gate added to model-onboarding pipeline to require IF-score >= 0.765 for hosted-safe rollout. This is currently set to allow int8 but block 4-bit until mitigation.

Model onboarding (product + infra touchpoints)
- Onboarding checklist updates: added quantization-profile metadata (quant-level, calibration-set-id, eval-run-id) to bundle manifest. Product and infra sign-off required before canary.
- Router fallback policy: suggested policy — prefer int8 on Premium & Dedicated; allow 4-bit on Dedicated-only pools with strict monitoring. Liam to prototype a policy that does dynamic selection based on per-request latency SLA and recent error-rate (owner: Liam).
- Observability: added new tracing tags for quant_level and calibration_id so Console dashboards can break down per-token cost & latency by quantized variant. Hook implemented in serving-runtime branch (PR 472).

Standups / syncs this week
- Mon standup: review of initial quant experiments. Consensus to prioritize int8 for Hosted API and keep 4-bit experimental in Dedicated.
- Wed deep-dive (1h): activation distribution plots showed attention head #7 and FFN block #2 have outsized dynamic ranges -> focused clipping recommended. Rafael to run layerwise bias-correction experiment.
- Fri sync with product: discussed SLA implications and rollout messaging for customers; product asked for a short one-pager describing expected tradeoffs (action: Aisha to draft by 2026-07-23).

Blockers / open questions
- Are we comfortable with a ~1.6% drop in IF-score for int8 on hosted? Product asked for clear customer-facing guidance. Suggested mitigation: enable int8 but expose a per-route flag to pin FP16 for latency-insensitive routes.
- Need to validate regression across more languages (currently most calibration/eval in English). Marta to coordinate multilingual eval subset selection (owner: Marta, due 2026-07-28).
- Cost model: updated per-token cost estimate for int8 looks promising but need to update billing pipeline to correctly attribute GPU utilization savings to customer invoices — flagged to finance (linked artifact CONFLUENCE-APPL-598).

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Try hybrid quantization: int8 for attention weights, 4-bit for feed-forward with bias-finetune — could give memory win w/o decoding instability. Worth a 2-day spike.
- Consider adding a "quality shadow" mode: send samples to FP16 model asynchronously for unseen failure patterns and log diffs. Might be heavy but useful for hard-to-detect hallucinations.

Action items (owner, due)
- Aisha: Draft product one-pager on int8 tradeoffs (2026-07-23).
- Rafael: Layerwise bias-fine-tune spike + open PR w/ activation logs (2026-07-29).
- Liam: Prototype latency-aware router policy for quant variants (2026-07-30).
- Marta: Build multilingual eval subset and run initial sweep (2026-07-28).
- Team: Add adversarial 50-prompt set to nightly evals (2026-07-24).

Quick links
- PR: serving-runtime/pull/472 (quant trace tags)
- Jira: JIRA-APPL-212 (regressions), JIRA-APPL-223 (onboarding checklist updates)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-APPL-598 (cost model notes)

Closing
- Overall progress is good. Int8 looks production-ready with minor documentation and routing work. 4-bit remains promising but needs more stability work and stronger eval coverage before any hosted rollout.
- Will reconvene in next weekly sync with extended eval results and Rafael's mitigation experiments.

-- end of notes --
